headline: **MLB Daily Recap: August 2, 2026**
article:
The Toronto Blue Jays took down the St. Louis Cardinals 5-1, with Kevin Gausman earning the win after 5.2 innings of work. In other action, the Seattle Mariners secured a 4-3 victory over the Minnesota Twins, with Randy Arozarena leading the Twins with 2 hits, including a home run, and 1 RBI in 4 at-bats. The Tampa Bay Rays secured a narrow victory over the Chicago White Sox, winning 1-0, with Drew Rasmussen leading the Rays' pitching effort. The Miami Marlins secured a 6-2 victory over the New York Mets, with Javier Sanoja hitting 2 home runs and driving in 2 runs in 5 at-bats.

Several players are dealing with injuries, including Will Klein of the Los Angeles Dodgers, who has been placed on the 15-day injured list due to right elbow discomfort. Jesus Rodriguez of the San Francisco Giants has been placed on the 10-day injured list with right elbow neuritis. Ryan O'Hearn of the Pittsburgh Pirates has been placed on the 10-day injured list with a left quad strain. Luke Raley of the Seattle Mariners has been placed on the 10-day injured list retroactive to July 31, 2026, with a left forearm strain. Mike Paredes of the Minnesota Twins has been transferred from the 15-day injured list to the 60-day injured list with a left oblique strain. Brock Stewart of the Los Angeles Dodgers has been placed on the 15-day injured list with right shoulder discomfort. Matt Vierling of the Detroit Tigers has been placed on the 10-day injured list retroactive to July 30, 2026, with a left adductor strain. J.P. Crawford of the Seattle Mariners has been placed on the 10-day injured list retroactive to July 30, 2026, with left wrist inflammation.

The Kansas City Royals have acquired right-handed pitcher Lucas Braun in a trade with the Atlanta Braves, sending outfielder Lane Thomas and left-handed pitcher Bailey Falter to Atlanta. The Seattle Mariners have traded right-handed pitcher Luis Castillo to the Chicago White Sox for right-handed pitcher Seranthony Domínguez, catcher Boston Smith, right fielder Nolan Jones, and cash.
